newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales off 0.4 pct Sept -- Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales off 0.4 pct Sept -- Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales fell 0.4 percent in the four weeks of fiscal September versus August, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index.

The index rose 4.8 percent when compared with the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales also rose 4.5 percent in the week ended September 28, compared with the same week a year ago, it said.

Strong, above-plan chain-store sales during the week were countered by slow growth rates at the department stores and unusual weakness among discounters, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.

"Wal-Mart tells us that they find people shopping on the basis of a bi-weekly payroll cycle, that is, people who get paid every other week," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
"If you get paid you go out and go shopping. If you haven't gotten paid that week, you don't shop," Eilenberg said, adding that Wal-Mart Stores Inc has been seeing ups-and-downs that way.
Eilenberg also noted that there has been a pickup in apparel sales in the chain stores and department stores.
"I think apparel is in for a decent fall season," he said. But he conceded that discounters have yet to see strength in apparels.
